question.knowledge_point: Evaluating an Integral Over an Interval of Length Zero
question.worked_solution:
Notice that the lower and upper limits are the same. So, the integral evaluates to zero:

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{-2}\frac{1}{1+{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x=0
$$
